ctx.x: This letter he is about to read now. I've come across it by accident. It will show a man how he spoke out of both sides of his mouth. 1949, he said that there was no other band. Now he's promoting Tom Brown, who is recording and who is a member, and got 30 pieces of silver in the form of a loving cup, like Judas Iscariot got when he sold Christ. Would you please read that article from Mr. Sushant?
All right. This is the letter. The heading is... No dating on it. Dr. Edmond Sushant. No all names there.

Dear Stuart, thought you'd like a copy of these snaps. Do wish that I could get some together with you and Tom Brown some night soon. And deeply, as it says here, I am deeply regretful that you got away without playing a note last Saturday night, even though you gave me that, quote, I got a new horn and can't blow it yet, unquote. I was not going to let you get away without showing those guys, well, they call you Red Hot. That's underlined from I was not going down through Red Hot. Speak to Tom some night soon…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: You have men like Marshall Stein, John Hammond, Dr. Sushaw, who's supposed to know about this music.

ctx.x: Now, I just showed you the kind of propaganda that the people put out. They all knew about Tiger Rag. Now, here's a Negro. I'm going to give you his record. And if I'm wrong, then the world is wrong. This Negro lived in Plaquemine, Louisiana, at the age of about six to eight years old, worked as a shoeshine boy for Ferdinand Herbert, who operated a barbershop in Plaquemine, Louisiana. He came to New Orleans in his late teens. He lies as to hearing Buddy Bowling play. From the dates given in the second line of…

No. It's going now. This is a letter. At the head is Dr. Admiral Sushaw, New Orleans. They, December 29, 1949. Dear Mr. LaRock, resuming our conversation of last night, I would simply write to repeat. The Marcus of Donegal wrote me and asked me to communicate to you. His address is, the Marcus of Donegal, 16 High Park Gate, London, SWF, England. As you know, Lord Donegal is head of all the jazz clubs of Great Britain. They're planning to have a 30-year centennial commemorating the opening up of the original Dixie…

Well, that'll go to show you how a man can speak out of both sides of his mouth. I received a letter. Now, there's been plenty going on after Marshall Steins had given Tom Brown this favorable write-up. Brown was to go to different papers and have this printed and show it as real history. This was lying history connived by this man, Marshall Steins, who somewhere along in the front of these reels, you'll read his letter that he admitted to me he was lying. Now, they come up with more lies. There's a man from…
